multi_facility._comment_distribution: Proportion of patients using 1, 2, or 3+ distinct facilities. Must sum to 1.0.
multi_facility._comment_outside_prob: Per encounter-type probability of the encounter occurring outside the patient's primary facility.
multi_facility._comment_geo_affinity: When an outside-facility encounter is generated, these weights control how strongly geographic proximity is preferred.
multi_facility._comment_adjacent_regions: Regions considered geographically adjacent for facility-selection affinity weighting.
multi_facility._comment_ed_ip_lock: ED→inpatient admission always stays at the same facility as the admitting ED (MF-008). Set false only for explicit interfacility-transfer modeling.
multi_facility._comment_mrn_prefix: Each facility MRN is prefixed with the facility code to make cross-facility collisions structurally impossible.

document_templates.note_template:
CHIEF COMPLAINT: {chief_complaint}

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: {patient_name} is a {age}-year-old {sex} with known sickle cell disease presenting for {chief_complaint}. Patient reports {compliance_statement}. Pain scale 7/10 in bilateral lower extremities and lower back. Denies chest pain or shortness of breath at rest.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Vitals: BP {bp} mmHg, HR {hr} bpm, Weight {weight} lbs
General: Appears uncomfortable, in moderate pain. Icteric sclerae noted.
Abdomen: Mild left upper quadrant tenderness. Spleen not palpable (autosplenectomy).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. {diagnosis} — {plan}
2. Pain management — IV hydration, analgesics as needed.

FOLLOW-UP: Return in 4-6 weeks or sooner if fever develops or pain escalates.

Recurrent vaso-occlusive pain crises requiring hospitalization

comments: Non-smoker; avoids respiratory irritants due to sickle cell disease.
Patient reports drinking 8-10 glasses of water daily to prevent crisis.
Maintains high hydration as advised to reduce sickling episodes.

rad_order_templates.reason_description: Evaluate for acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease
result_texts: New bilateral lower lobe opacities consistent with acute chest syndrome. Recommend hematology consult.
No acute cardiopulmonary process. No pleural effusion. Cardiac silhouette mildly enlarged.
Patchy airspace opacities in right lower lobe. Clinical correlation with fever and pain crisis advised.

rad_order_templates.reason_description: Evaluate for stroke or CNS vasculopathy in sickle cell disease
result_texts: Multiple small foci of T2/FLAIR signal abnormality in bilateral subcortical white matter consistent with prior small vessel infarcts.
No acute intracranial abnormality. No diffusion restriction to suggest acute infarct.
Mild diffuse cerebral atrophy. Small chronic lacunar infarcts noted in the basal ganglia bilaterally.
